cards.text: New letter, friend! Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the church of God in Corinth and to all the saints throughout Achaia. And he didn't write this one solo, because there's a second name right next to his at the top, like a group card at work.

cards.question: Paul writes this letter to the church in Corinth together with ___ our brother.

cards.text: Then the greeting, and Paul skips the "hope this letter finds you well" small talk. Just grace and peace, and he says exactly who it's from.

cards.question: True or false: Paul sends the Corinthians grace and peace from himself and Timothy.

cards.text: Most of us open an email and go STRAIGHT to the problem. Paul bursts into praise: "Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort…"
And Paul says God comforts us in ALL our troubles, not some but ALL. The big ones, the messy ones, the staring-at-the-ceiling-at-two-in-the-morning ones.

cards.question: Paul says God comforts us in all our troubles. Why, according to Paul?

answers.text: So we can comfort others in trouble
So we never face trouble again
So we can rest from all our work

cards.text: Then Paul lines up two things that both overflow, like my bowl when I get a little too happy with the chocolate chips. First, he says the sufferings of Christ overflow to us.

cards.question: Paul says that just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, through Christ our ___ overflows.

cards.text: Now Paul looks at both sides of it: being afflicted and being comforted. He says BOTH are for somebody.

cards.question: Paul says being afflicted and being comforted both serve somebody's comfort. Whose comfort?
Paul tells the Corinthians that when we are afflicted, it is for their comfort and their ___.
True or false: Paul says the Corinthians' comfort produces patient endurance in them as they go through the same sufferings.
Paul tells the Corinthians, "And our hope for you is sure…" Why?

answers.text: They share in our sufferings and will share our comfort
Timothy brought us good news about every one of them
They have held on to everything we taught them

cards.text: Then Paul tells the Corinthians about "the hardships we encountered in the province of Asia." No thumbs-up emoji and "I'm fine" from Paul, friend. He tells it STRAIGHT.

cards.question: About those hardships in the province of Asia, Paul says, "We were under a burden…" How heavy was that burden?

answers.text: Far beyond our ability to endure
Enough to make us stop preaching
Enough to send us back home

cards.question: True or false: Paul writes that under that burden, "…we despaired even of life."

cards.text: Paul says, "Indeed, we felt we were under the sentence of death…" That's heavy, friend.

cards.question: Paul writes that it felt like a sentence of death, in order that we would not trust in ___.
Paul says the point was to trust in God, even facing death. What does Paul say this God does?

cards.text: And God came through, friend. Paul says, "He has delivered us from such a deadly peril…"

cards.question: True or false: After that rescue, Paul says not to count on God to deliver again.

cards.text: Paul says, "In Him we have placed our hope that He will yet again deliver us…" And he doesn't leave the Corinthians on the bench. He puts them in the game.

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians they help in this by their ___.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "…many will give thanks on our behalf for the favor shown us in answer to their prayers." It's like a kitchen where everybody who helped stir the dough gets to cheer when the cookies come out of the oven!
